summary: Phare du Borgot at L'Étang-du-Nord, Magdalen Islands: a keeper's house lit in 1874, a steel tower from 1967, the fibreglass tower of 1987; the light's end is disputed (2011 or 2015).

structures.note: Two storeys with a lantern on the roof (heritage sources); a square wooden building 28 ft high with an attached dwelling (LighthouseFriends). Focal plane 200 ft; visible 20 miles (LighthouseFriends). Restored 1913 per the heritage sources; demolished 1967 per the heritage sources, razed in the 1970s per LighthouseFriends.
Steel tower of 1967 (heritage sources), demolished 1987 per the Secteur entry
Heritage register says plastic; the Society and Les amis des phares say fibreglass. Octagonal lantern painted red.

access.note: Grounds open; the tower is closed (LighthouseFriends). An observation site has been laid out around the tower for visitors, on chemin du Phare (heritage register; the Society calls it well maintained). No source says the tower may be climbed.

visit.note: Observation site around the tower; grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three accounts disagree: the Society and Radio-Canada say the light went out in 2011; LighthouseFriends (and Rowlett) say 2015; the heritage register says it is still working. Not resolved. The record's 2015 is one of the three.
The register and the Society credit the municipality with the 2006 citation; Radio-Canada credits the Quebec government. The story gives both.

LighthouseFriends gives Timothy O'Brien as first keeper (1874-1891); the Society and Radio-Canada give Néciphore/Nicéphore Arsenault as keeper 1874-1921. The 1891 Department appointment of Nectaire Arseneau at Étang-du-Nord is on the page image. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the first-keeper question is open. LighthouseFriends gives Timothy O'Brien 1874 to 1891 and then Nectaire Arseneau from the Department's 1891 appointment; the Society and Radio-Canada give Néciphore/Nicéphore Arsenault 1874 to 1921 as the sole keeper, which conflicts with the 1891 appointment. Not merged. The Turnbull and McKay/Mackay lists differ in years and spelling, and the story reports both. The Department's 1903 lightkeepers list (printed p. 211, scan p. 224) was checked on the page image: Arseneau, Nectaire, Etang du Nord, July 21, 1891 is one row, with the Quebec 'Between Montreal and Quebec and below Quebec' heading above it. Light status: 2011 (Society, Radio-Canada), 2015 (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett), still working (register). The record's deactivated 2015 is one of these three; the Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights (A1488) was not read and would settle it. Characteristic Fl W 6s, focal height 28 m, and the tower's range in the record come from Wikidata and the French Wikipedia; neither was cited, so the facts omit them. Units: the 1874 focal plane (200 ft) and range (twenty miles, not stated as nautical) are given in metres and km in the story, with the source's feet and miles in parentheses. Heritage citation: the register and the Society say the municipality; Radio-Canada says the Quebec government. Ownership: the record's agency is the Government of Canada; LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns it. Radio-Canada says the Canadian government owns it and has judged it surplus. The record's 'automated 1987' conflicts with LighthouseFriends' 1970s automation; the story gives the 1970s, from LF and the register. The steel tower's demolition is 1987 (Secteur entry) against LighthouseFriends' razing of the wooden house in the 1970s; both are stated. The 1913 work: the heritage register and the Society say the house was restored; LighthouseFriends says a new dwelling and lantern were built 1912 to 1913. Material of the current tower: plastic (register) or fibreglass (Society, Route). The 1898 fire and the 1988 wreck come from LighthouseFriends; the travel-site account of the towlines is secondary. The wartime submarine report (Society; Radio-Canada) names no dated record. French sources are translated; where a sentence rests on the French, the English rendering is ours. Wikipedia (French) was read for leads only and is not cited. No photos supplied. People who may be alive (keepers ending after 1960) are named only as the published sources name them, in their public role.
